summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion from Al-Wajeez on the rulings of menstruation and postpartum bleeding in Islamic jurisprudence. He explains that postpartum bleeding (nifas) has no minimum duration but a maximum of 40 days, after which a woman's legal status changes regardless of continued bleeding. Sh. Ali Mashhour outlines five prohibitions for a menstruating or postpartum woman: prayer, fasting, reciting the Quran, handling the physical Mushaf, and sexual intercourse. He clarifies exceptions and alternatives, noting that reading Quranic text from electronic devices, handling a translation, or using gloves when touching the Mushaf are permissible options.
